summary: Feed s139_double is degraded: IDS sees 19.0% one-way TCP sessions (needs both directions) and 2.37 Gbps bursts overload its 1 Gbps port (237% capacity). Both cause detection gaps.

findings.root_cause: 24 of 126 TCP sessions (19.0%, threshold 10%) show only one direction. Classic visibility gap from SPAN/TAP or packet broker not aggregating both directions to the same IDS port - either SPAN configured for Tx or Rx only, asymmetric routing with single-homed capture, or hash-based load-balancing splitting client->server and server->client across different tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly and stateful signature matching. One-way flows prevent stream reassembly, break flow tracking and bidirectional signatures, causing missed intrusions and high false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session to the same IDS tool port using bidirectional-aware hashing/aggregation on the packet broker, and verify SPAN/TAP captures both Tx and Rx. Ensures IDS sees full handshake and payload in both directions.

findings.root_cause: Peak 2.37 Gbps in 1 ms burst vs 1 Gbps IDS port (237% of capacity, 3 overloaded intervals). Aggregate feed rate exceeds tool port speed; packet broker is forwarding line-rate bursts without load-balancing, filtering, or rate-limiting.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port is oversubscribed by 2.37x. Tool NIC will drop packets indiscriminately during bursts, creating random detection holes, missed exploits, and incomplete flow logs even for correctly aggregated sessions.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3x 1 Gbps IDS ports (or upgrade to 10 Gbps) with bidirectional-consistent load balancing so no single port exceeds 80% utilization, preserving packet delivery during bursts while keeping both directions of a flow together.
